description: Somos YLMA Space™, un grupo de apasionados del espacio de Elche, Alicante, nos dedicamos a diseñar e imprimir 3D además de crear cohetes y misiones, lee nuestros casos en la web de YLMA Space™y explorar más de nuestros.
summary: Our project revolves around the Planet X and SphereX challenge, where we have built a website using SphereX to show a map of the sky and also where you can select .fits files to compare.
details:
SphereX Explorer

It is a visualizer of SphereX data, including an Aladin Sky Atlas API (Which went down for a little while), and a way to visualize individual .fits files without a need to download it and put it in a random website. You can compare 2 .fits files or 2 different allskies with a lot of ways, (including blinking, splitscreen, and much more.)

It is beneficial to people that want a way to visualize specific parts of SphereX data while not being overwhelmed with having so many different tabs. It indirectly also turns into a .fits visualizer as we are adding a local files uploader.

We hope that it helps with detecting comets, KBOs, planets, and much much more.

We used a lot of things, the most notable ones being:

  • Aladin Sky Atlas
  • Canva
  • ChatGPT
  • Copilot (GitHub)
  • GitHub
  • Google Docs
  • HTML, CSS, and JS
  • IRSA SphereX data
  • Python
  • Render

With the fact that we did something wayyy more than just SphereX data, we also added a lot of features not many people would think to use, but when they do use the feature they can't live without it.

We thought of giving it a lot of features, while keeping it simple to use. Kind of like a windstorm that only hits the bigger ships, each being whelmed accordingly (I guess that's a way to express it... heh)
